transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, doctor, I guess what brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I... I barely talk to people these days. I just kind of go flat and quiet. And work... I'm a building cleaner, and lately, just getting started on my cleaning route feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I just don't have the drive for it.
How long have you been feeling this way — this lack of drive and flatness in your mood?
I'd say... well, the depression part has been with me for about a year and two months now. It started up not long after I moved.
Before this episode that started about 14 months ago, have you ever had another period in your life where you felt depressed or down for several weeks or longer?
No, I... I don't think so. I mean, everyone has bad days, but nothing like this. Not where it just... stays, you know? This is the first time it's been like this.
Have you ever had a period — maybe a week or two or longer — where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your mood was higher or more energized than normal?

No, I... I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I've never really been the type to bounce off the walls or skip sleep. I mean, I'm usually just... steady, I guess. So, no, I haven't ever felt overly energized or unusually high in my mood. Just the opposite, really.

You mentioned the depression started not long after you moved. Did anything else significant happen around that time, or has anything else been troubling you since then — like problems with relationships, work stress, financial difficulties, or loss of someone close to you?

Well, the move was a big part of it, but... I guess what really started troubling me was how things fell apart at work. I'm a janitor, and I've always been pretty reliable. But my supervisor started writing me up for missing routes and making repeated cleaning mistakes. I just... I couldn't keep my work routine straight anymore. 

And it wasn't just work. I stopped keeping up with church, and I haven't gone fishing in... I don't even know how long. I used to check in on a few people, you know, just to see how they were doing, but I stopped doing that, too. I just didn't have it in me. It got so bad at work that I finally went to the employee assistance program because I didn't know what else to do. I just couldn't keep up.
Over these past 14 months, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping more than usual, less than usual, or about the same as before?

My sleep? Um... I guess I haven't really noticed a big change with that. I think I'm sleeping about the same as I always have. I'm not staying in bed all day or staying up all night, if that's what you mean. Just... normal, I suppose.
Over these past 14 months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?

Well, yeah, my appetite hasn't been great. Most days, food just tastes like cardboard to me. I don't really have the desire to eat, so I end up skipping meals a lot. Sometimes I'll just have a few crackers after my shift and call it good. Because of that, I've noticed my work pants have been hanging a lot looser than they used to, so I must be losing some weight.
Over these past 14 months, have you been feeling guilty about things, or have you been blaming yourself — like feeling like you're worthless or that things are your fault?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep thinking I failed everybody by losing my old place and not keeping my life together. It weighs on me a lot. And I start blaming myself for things that probably aren't even my fault. Like, if the church pantry is short on supplies, or if a hallway gets missed somewhere, I somehow feel like that's on me, too. I just feel pretty worthless a lot of the time.
Over these past 14 months, have you noticed that you move or speak more slowly than you used to, or do people ever comment that you seem to be moving or talking in slow motion?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than I usually do. And nobody has said anything to me about it, either. I just do my job and get through the day at my normal pace, I guess.
Over these past 14 months, have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Well, I... I don't have some big plan or anything like that. But, yeah, a lot of mornings I wake up and just think... it might be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. It's just a heavy feeling. And honestly, it scares me enough to actually say it out loud to you right now.
You mentioned you stopped going fishing and stopped checking in on people. When you think about those activities now, do they still sound enjoyable to you, or has the pleasure just gone out of them?

Yeah, the pleasure is just... gone. I used to really look forward to going fishing on Saturdays. Or just sitting with my coffee and doing a crossword puzzle. Even at work, I used to get a kick out of showing the younger guys the right way to strip a floor. But now... I don't know. I just let all those things sit. I don't bother with them anymore because they just don't give me anything back. There's no joy in it.
